title: Why the Jazz Workshop began: no schools, only clubs and jam sessions
summary: Turbinton says the 1969 workshop grew out of young musicians' frustration at having no place to learn improvisation, only late-night jam sessions in drug-and-alcohol clubs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Okay, we're here to talk about the New Orleans Jazz Workshop from 1969. I guess we'll start out by maybe talking about just exactly how the workshop started and address kind of the

milieu of what was happening there. Well, the period that the Jazz Workshop developed and... Well, the time that... I mean... Sorry, go ahead. Sorry. The period that we developed the Jazz Workshop was one that was born out of frustration for myself and many of the young jazz musicians during that period of time. And that there were no schools in this immediate area or schools that we knew about to learn more about the techniques of improvisation as far as chord scale relationship. It was pretty much trial and error by going out and sitting in and jam sessions and being out very late hours in clubs and after all places where we would play sometimes after a regular engagement. There were places like Hollies and Birdland and a few other places that would play from, say, 3 to 7 in the morning after Friday night and Saturday night. And this was a traditional thing that happened. But it still was very competitive, but no formal guidelines as far as how to get from point A to B more clearly or more expediently without a lot of hanging out. And the environment was one thing that I thought was not conducive to the development of a young person to be in nightclub or alcohol and other drug-filled environments, which at that particular period of time generally permeated the whole atmosphere.
